figures.finding: The CNMI's income tax (the NMTIT) is built on the same tax laws and rates as the United States, filed with the CNMI Division of Revenue and Taxation, plus local taxes; a bona fide resident files one return, with the CNMI, on worldwide income.

value.administeredBy: CNMI Division of Revenue and Taxation

figures.applies: Bona fide residents of the CNMI

sources.said: The CNMI has its own tax system based partly on the same tax laws and tax rates that apply to the United States and partly on local taxes imposed by the CNMI government. … If you are a U.S. citizen, resident alien, or nonresident alien and a bona fide resident of the CNMI during the tax year, file your income tax return with the CNMI. Include income from worldwide sources on your CNMI return.

figures.finding: On top, the CNMI charges a wage and salary tax (and an earnings tax on self-employment) on annual amounts: nothing to $1,000, then 2% to $5,000, 3%, 4%, 5%, 6%, 7%, 8% and 9% above $50,000, each rate applied to the whole amount; it is credited against the NMTIT on CNMI-source income.

figures.finding: NMTIT on CNMI-source income, after those local taxes are credited, is rebated: 90% of a rebate base up to $20,000, $18,000 plus 70% of the excess to $100,000, and $74,000 plus 50% above.

figures.finding: Self-employment income connected with a CNMI business is reported to the United States on Form 1040-SS for self-employment tax, so US social security applies.

sources.said: Self-employment tax. If you have no U.S. filing requirement, but have income that is effectively connected with a trade or business in the CNMI, you must file Form 1040-SS with the United States to report your self-employment income and, if necessary, pay self-employment tax.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year and the 2025 return is due by 15 April 2026.
